suggestions.title: Step on the scale tomorrow morning — one read re-anchors the trend and grades the whoosh

rationale.science: A single weigh-in is noise, but a trend needs a fresh anchor to mean anything — and regular morning weigh-ins are one of the best-evidenced habits in weight management (Steinberg 2015). Your app already priced this gap itself: six missed mornings have widened its measured rate to 0.15–1.13 lb/wk.
rationale.data: Last read 8/21: 162.4, trend 162.9 — a record low, now carried six days on nothing. The 8/19 precedent: this same ask converted inside 24 hours.
rationale.relationship: One morning read collapses that rate interval back to a number and settles the giveback watch: a trend at or under 163.5 confirms last week's drop as fat, not water. Mid-162s is on script. Nothing else tonight can move that verdict.

suggestions.predict: A read lands within a day or two and the trend prints 162s, confirming the whoosh. Blank branch, named at filing: no read by 9/01 and the whoosh watch files VOID.

suggestions.title: Fill last Friday and Saturday's food — the weekend bet voids Sunday 8/30

rationale.science: When a rate looks slow, the first check is the log, not the metabolism (Alhassan 2008) — and a week that isn't on paper can't be checked at all.
rationale.data: Food logging stops at 8/20. The bet's two legs — 8/21 and 8/22, each over 2,600 — are still blank, along with every day since. The fill-in habit was seven-for-seven inside 24 hours before this week's first miss.
rationale.relationship: Two rough numbers grade a standing forecast honestly: over 2,600 both and my read of your weekends stands; under 2,500 both and I over-fit and will say so. No fill by Sunday and it files VOID — which teaches neither of us anything.

suggestions.predict: Both legs land by Saturday and the bet finally grades on its letter. Blank branch, already filed: still blank Sunday 8/30 → VOID, recorded as a design lesson, not a win or a loss.

suggestions.title: Put the training week on paper either way — sessions if they happened, a rest week if they didn't

rationale.science: A layoff of a week or two doesn't measurably cost a trained lifter muscle or strength, especially with protein kept high (Bosquet 2013; Ogasawara 2013). A sick week off reads as recovery, not damage.
rationale.data: Your last session is 8/21 — 'didn't feel great, left early' — after 8/20's 'was sick the past few days'. Six-plus days without a session is the longest gap in your file; the previous longest was four.
rationale.relationship: If you trained unlogged, the entries keep every ladder honest — rear-delt's two-skip watch and four fresh baselines are waiting on the next real sessions. If you rested, one line saying so converts a scary-looking blank into what it probably was: a deload after being sick. Then the first session back gets read as a comeback against baselines, not a decline against last month's peaks.

suggestions.predict: A session entry or an explicit rest-week note lands within three days, and the first session back opens at 1–2 reps in reserve and meets or resets its lines without any hold flags.
